candidates.buyer: Small villa, apartment and guest-house owners and Airbnb/Vrbo hosts, plus property managers (unverified count; thousands of properties per press)
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
candidates.evidence: https://www.barbadosparliament.com/uploads/bill_resolution/9b2c3cd242c5826d62c231b55e59201b.pdf ; https://barbadostoday.bb/2025/09/17/govt-moves-to-bring-airbnb-short-term-rentals-into-regulatory-fold ; https://barbadostoday.bb/2025/09/26/wise-pause-to-rethink-tourist-accommodation-bill/ ; https://nationnews.com/?p=372005 (reports House passage, 2026) ; https://www.tourism.gov.bb/News/Press-Releases/Town-Hall-Meeting-On-New-Tourist-A. Petition by online renters Sep 2025 shows many small hosts and strong feeling.
candidates.existing: The competitor search (English, 'licence guest records software operators') found no Barbados-specific tool; generic channel managers and PMS products exist but nothing built for the BTPA licence. The study's K04 levy tool idea was killed because platforms collect the levy; this is a different duty (licence, inspection, records), which the platforms do not handle.
candidates.known_note: Different duty from K04 (levy filing); same broad buyer group.
candidates.name: Tourist Accommodation Act licence and guest-record kit for villas, guest houses and small short-term-rental hosts
candidates.trigger: Tourist Accommodation Bill/Act 2025-26: licence, classification and registration with the Barbados Tourism Product Authority, inspection, two-year licence renewal, guest records, itemised invoices. Fines up to BBD 250,000. Earlier drafts: six-month grace for first-time applicants and five years for accessibility upgrades.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Act has received Senate passage, assent and a commencement date; final licence fee, renewal and guest-record rules; BTPA application portal; how many properties; whether hosts pay for compliance help rather than doing it themselves.

candidates.buyer: Private pharmacies and drug importers/storers (count unverified; probably fewer than a few hundred)
candidates.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
candidates.existing: Competitor search not run (score below 4). Pharmacies already use dispensing/POS systems; none checked for Barbados regulatory modules.
candidates.name: Medical Products Act 2026 transition kit for private pharmacies (premises certification, three-year renewal, licence tracking)
candidates.trigger: Barbados Medical Products Act 2026 (Act 2026-12): existing pharmacies must apply for premises certification within six weeks of commencement (s.21(5)); certificates run to 31 Dec of the third year; licences needed to import (s.37), store (s.39), manufacture (s.31), repackage (s.32), export (s.40); antimicrobial prescription records kept one year (s.34(5)). Commencement by proclamation (s.80).
candidates.unchecked: Commencement date; pharmacy count; whether Authority will run its own online portal; any recurring return or controlled-drug register in the regulations; competitor software.

candidates.buyer: Small employers who pay hourly or daily staff monthly; possibly household employers (unverified)
candidates.existing: Payroll packages and bureaus (see K06). This is a pay-cycle change, which any payroll tool handles.
candidates.known_note: Adjacent to K02/K06 payroll ideas but a different duty (pay frequency); likely folded into existing payroll tools.
candidates.name: Protection of Wages Act 2026 weekly/fortnightly pay and deduction-remittance helper for small employers
candidates.trigger: Protection of Wages Act 2026-15 (assented 7 Aug 2026; commencement by proclamation): pay at least weekly for hourly/daily/weekly wages, fortnightly for fortnightly wages; tougher penalties for deductions not passed on.
candidates.unchecked: Commencement date; whether wage statements or registers are required; whether domestic workers are covered.

candidates.buyer: Real estate agents, dealers in precious metals and stones, accountants and attorneys that are DNFBPs
candidates.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
candidates.evidence: https://barbadostoday.bb/2024/10/19/anti-money-laundering-registry-needed-for-non-financial-businesses/amp ; https://gisbarbados.gov.bb/?p=579893 ; https://nationnews.com/?p=171203 (BEVA lobbying; real estate unlicensed) ; https://governmentprintery.gov.bb/category/part-a/acts/ (Act 2026-24 title).
candidates.existing: Generic AML tools (Arctic Intelligence, Waystone guides) appear in results; no Barbados-specific DNFBP tool seen.
candidates.known_note: Overlaps the dealer side of K03 (precious metals) but adds real estate agents and other DNFBPs, with an AML-programme duty instead of a transaction register.
candidates.name: DNFBP AML registration and compliance programme for real estate agents, precious-metal dealers and small professional firms
candidates.trigger: MLFT (Prevention and Control) Act Second Schedule; AMLA Compliance Unit (Office of the Attorney General) supervises; registry for DNFBPs reported missing in Oct 2024, working group drafting sector guidelines; Money Laundering amendment Act 2026-24 passed 28 Sep 2026 (content unread).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the registry is live; what Act 2026-24 requires; any periodic return; number of firms.

candidates.buyer: Small CSPs, accountants and law firms; companies, SRLs, limited partnerships, external companies
candidates.category: 31. Beneficial ownership register (Beneficial Ownership Transparency and Register Act 2026)
candidates.existing: Law-firm and CSP alerts (Vistra, Trident) only; no tool found.
candidates.known_note: New evidence for K01: the Act is now in force (1 Sep 2026) with a first filing deadline near end Nov 2026. Worth a re-score by the verification stage; not re-checked here.
candidates.name: Beneficial Ownership Transparency and Register Act 2026 first filing and annual confirmation
candidates.trigger: Act 2026-16 in force 1 Sep 2026; first filing within three months (around end Nov 2026), annual confirmation in anniversary month; fees via S.I. 2026 No. 81.

candidates.buyer: Security guard agencies and private investigators
candidates.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
candidates.existing: None seen. Renewals handled manually by the PMO Investigation Unit.
candidates.name: Private security guard, investigator and agency annual licence renewal tracker
candidates.trigger: Private Investigators and Security Guards Act Cap. 372: renew by 30 Jan each year with Police Certificate of Character (valid six months); fines up to BBD 5,000 or two years.
candidates.unchecked: Number of agencies (probably dozens); any in-year reporting; clients' duty to check licences.

candidates.buyer: Private day care centres and family day care homes
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
candidates.name: Private day care and family day care annual registration and monthly statistics pack
candidates.trigger: Child Care Board Act 1981-34 and Private Child Care Centre Regulations: registration by 31 Jan yearly with Fire Service, health and food licence, staff medical, food handler and police certificates; monthly statistics to the Board.
candidates.unchecked: Number of centres; whether statistics are filed online; staff-certificate expiry tracking pain.

candidates.buyer: Minibus, ZR and route taxi owners
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Transport Authority has its own online permit pages.
candidates.name: ZR, minibus and route taxi permit and licence-to-drive tracking
candidates.trigger: Transport Authority Act Cap. 295A permits; 2024 fees order (application BBD 100; minibus licence BBD 150; route taxi BBD 155 per search summary).
candidates.unchecked: Renewal cycle, vehicle inspection and insurance deadlines; count of operators.

candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.name: Pesticide buyer licence and dealer record keeping
candidates.trigger: Pesticides Control Act and Regulations 1974; Dec 2020 plan to license buyers of products such as Roundup.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the buyer licence was ever introduced; retailer count; any sales register.

candidates.category: 35. Data Protection Act 2019 registration of controllers
candidates.existing: Consultancy and generic privacy tools only.
candidates.name: Data Protection Act controller and processor registration
candidates.trigger: Sections 50-57 of the Data Protection Act 2019 were excluded from commencement in 2021, pending proclamation.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the registration sections were proclaimed after 2023; deadline; fees. Generic compliance product risk.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic Employees Act Cap. 344 (old, limited rules, overtime record duty). No NIS household-employer guidance or portal found. New Protection of Wages Act 2026 (Act 2026-15, assented 7 Aug 2026, commencement by proclamation) sets weekly/fortnightly pay; whether it covers domestic workers is unverified. Nothing strong; household-employer payroll is thin (see K02/K06).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Precious Metals and Second Hand Metals Act 2013 (licence from district Magistrate, registered with Commissioner of Police within 7 days, Customs inspection of exports). Same buyer and duty as K03. Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Covered by the 2013 Act for metals/jewellery (K03). Separate pawnbroker rules not found; nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Cash-for-gold firms are licensed under the 2013 Act; police warned unlicensed ones (K03). The DNFBP AML regime for dealers in precious metals and stones is also pending (see candidate on DNFBP registry). Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Budget; no Barbados source searched.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Veterinary Services import permits under Animals (Diseases and Importation) Act Cap. 253; per-shipment permits and quarantine. Per-event, low volume, no recurring register found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Budget; the vet search returned no abattoir licensing source.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Only import-permit material found. The Barbados Medical Products Act 2026 repeals the Therapeutic Substances Act and adds licences for importing and storing drugs and a register of poison sellers; whether this reaches vet medicines is unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Barbados Water Authority supplies the island almost entirely; no small-system regime expected. Not searched.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides Control Act and Regulations 1974: Board licenses imports, approves products and labels. In Dec 2020 the Minister announced a buyer licence plan; implementation unverified. Small buyer group, state-run.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Budget; not searched separately (security agencies screened under 26).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Budget; not searched. A Protection of Depositors Act 2026 and a Money Laundering amendment (Act 2026-24) appeared in the Gazette list but were not read.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Transport Authority Act Cap. 295A: permits for minibus, ZR and route taxi, with new, transfer and status pages online; 2024 fees order. No renewal deadline or compliance pain found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K07 (street vendors). Money changers not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Private day care centres and family day care: annual Child Care Board registration by 31 Jan with Fire Service certificate, Ministry of Health food licence, staff medicals, food handler and police character certificates; monthly statistics to the Board. Small pool and a state-run process. Other sub-types not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Maximum retail prices are set by regulation (Miscellaneous Controls (Control of Prices) (General) Regulations, amended Feb 2026, effective 2 Mar 2026) and adjusted by the Ministry. No dealer licence or reporting source found; state sets prices, so few pain points.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No meaningful commodity trading sector in Barbados; not searched.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: FSC supervises 25 registered credit unions (July 2024 list) under the FSC Act 2010 and Co-operative Societies Act Cap. 378A; FSC Amendment and Validation Act 2026-22 exists but was not read. Too few buyers. Friendly societies and the co-operatives registrar not found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: No private clinic licence or insurer-reporting source found. Health Services (Amendment) Act 2025-9 listed but not read. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Barbados Medical Products Act 2026 (Act 2026-12, Gazette 22 Jun 2026): new Medical Products Authority; pharmacy premises certification and a Register of Pharmacies; licences for import, storage, export and manufacture; commencement by proclamation (s.80); existing pharmacies must apply within six weeks of commencement (s.21(5)); certificates run three years. Private pharmacists still reviewing the Act.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private Investigators and Security Guards Act Cap. 372: guards, investigators and agencies must renew licences by 30 Jan each year with a Police Certificate of Character, handled by the PMO Investigation Unit. Small pool, manual renewal. Cleaning and manpower agencies not found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: DNFBP supervision sits with the AMLA Compliance Unit (Office of the Attorney General) under the Second Schedule of the MLFT Act; an Oct 2024 report said no DNFBP registry existed yet, and a working group is drafting sector guidelines. Real estate agents have no statutory licence: BEVA is lobbying for one. A Money Laundering amendment Act 2026-24 (28 Sep 2026) exists, unread. No recurring return found yet.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourist Accommodation Bill 2025 (BTPA): licensing, classification, registration and inspection of all tourist accommodation including villas and short-term rentals; two-year licences, guest records, itemised invoices, fines up to BBD 250,000. Introduced Sep 2025, paused, sent to a Senate Joint Select Committee 3 Dec 2025, reported passed by the House in 2026. Assent and commencement unconfirmed. The levy side is K04 (rejected).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Customs broker licences under Customs Act Cap. 66 regs 183-185; April 2026 low-value import change; draft customs bill status unknown. Fish: Fisheries Act Cap. 391 vessel licensing, plus a mandatory vessel re-marking exercise (8P numbers, 1,156 registered boats). Nothing recurring that software could serve.

coverage.category: 31. Beneficial ownership register (Beneficial Ownership Transparency and Register Act 2026)
coverage.found: Act 2026-16 in force 1 Sep 2026; existing companies, SRLs, limited partnerships and external companies must file within three months (about end Nov 2026), then confirm annually in the incorporation-anniversary month. Fees in S.I. 2026 No. 81. This is K01.

coverage.category: 32. Protection of Wages Act 2026
coverage.found: Act 2026-15, assented 7 Aug 2026, commencement by proclamation. Employers paying hourly or daily staff monthly must move to weekly or fortnightly pay; wire transfers recognised; tougher penalties for unremitted deductions. Labour Department is running employer seminars. Statement and record duties not confirmed.

coverage.category: 33. Medical Products Act 2026 (pharmacies, importers, poison sellers)
coverage.found: See category 25.

coverage.category: 34. Tourist Accommodation Bill 2025/26
coverage.found: See category 29.

coverage.category: 35. Data Protection Act 2019 registration of controllers
coverage.found: Sections 50-57 (registers of data controllers and processors) were excluded from the March 2021 start, per DataGuidance Oct 2023. No later proclamation found, so no live deadline.

coverage.category: 36. Fisheries Act vessel registration and licensing
coverage.found: See category 30. Fisheries Policy 2023-2033 plans enhanced vessel and fisherfolk licensing.

coverage.category: 37. Security guard and investigator agency licensing
coverage.found: See category 26.

coverage.category: 38. Money laundering and depositor protection Acts 2026 (Acts 2026-20, 2026-24)
coverage.found: Titles seen in the Gazette list only; texts not read for small-business duties.
